Stage 2 of our journey · Synthetic test system: 450 wells

Scenario explorer: what if pumping or rain changes?

This tool runs on our 450-well test system. Pick a simulated well, choose how much it pumps and how wet the season is, and see how its water level responds, based on what the model learned from six months of simulated data.

What you can do here

Choose a well, how far ahead to look, and "what-if" settings for pumping and rain. The page shows the projected level and how much each choice moves it.

Keep in mind

This is a simulated system. Future weather follows an assumed seasonal calendar, not a weather forecast. Beyond 30 days the shaded range is an extrapolation, and in testing it proved somewhat too narrow.

Why it matters

It shows the kind of "what if we pump less?" question a well operator could ask once real long-term data is available. See where this fits.

The model learns daily movement from pumping, learned delayed raw rainfall, municipal supply, demand, and the previous level change.

Forecast checkpoints

CheckpointDateExpected level80% range

Rainfall delay is learned from raw rain using days 121–150. Future drivers follow a synthetic 365-day calendar including monsoon assumptions; they are not weather forecasts. Bands target 80% on inner validation but cover 63.0% on the final fleet test; beyond 30 days their square-root growth is extrapolated.

Borewell Forecast is a proof of concept for forecasting groundwater levels in Bengaluru borewells. Results are labelled by where the data came from: vendor export (15 days, July 2026, in the vendor's real format but with demonstration water-level values), synthetic test system (450 simulated wells with a known answer) or digital twin (a physics-based simulation of the 579 wells over a year). No real water-level measurement has been used yet, and nothing here is yet a validated field forecast.
